ruling: The ordering runs: (1) enforcement triggers jurisdiction-differentiated segmentation, (2) compute and research effort concentrate in the unfrozen branch, (3) once self-improvement is measurable, the resulting cycle-time compression makes the frozen/disclosed branch's capability lag the live branch's by a growing, dated margin.
because: Every round-2 DEFEND held its stage-1 claim rather than conceding, so segmentation-under-enforcement is common ground; the actual dispute is what stage 2 does with it. Five of seven minutes (lab-moves, ai-public-backlash, ai-regulation-teeth, ai-oversight-lag, and ai-pressure by implication) converge on capability-gap widening as the live threat, while pressure-model alone argues the compressed cycle changes disclosure-staleness rather than the branch choice itself — this is a genuine second thread, not noise, since it targets the audit/regulator relationship rather than the lab/market relationship.
threat_live: A standing, self-widening capability gap between the disclosed/frozen branch and the undisclosed/live branch becomes possible once self-improvement is measurable — the freeze date stops being a snapshot and becomes a vintage stamp, because the compressed cycle means the gap compounds rather than staying fixed.
strongest_minute: ai-oversight-lag — it is the only minute that locates the mechanism in the audit channel itself (sampling only the disclosed branch) rather than restating the capability-gap outcome, giving a distinct causal reason the gap would persist rather than just asserting it does.
weakest_minute: ai-pressure — its round-1 claim already concedes the compressed-cycle evidence surfaces 'first and most visibly' in the non-enforcing market, which is the same capability-gap observation as five other minutes wearing different words, and round 2 adds no independent mechanism, just a defense against pressure-model's sharper version.
shared_assumption: All seven minutes assume the lab responds to enforcement by bifurcating its release architecture rather than by slowing down uniformly or exiting the enforcing market — none argues for this over the alternative, they inherit it from the stage-1 brief.
smuggled_assumption: pressure-model smuggles a second assumption the brief did not grant: that a specific regulator (EU AI Office or a BIS-tied body) will act on the staleness signal by publicly flagging it, which imports an institutional-response claim beyond the granted branch of lab behavior.
unresolved: Whether the compressed cycle changes which branch the lab favors (majority view: gap widens because effort concentrates in the live branch) or only changes the cadence mismatch between disclosure and deployment (pressure-model's view, which keeps branch choice constant) — the minutes argue past each other on this rather than resolving it.
